sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Lakshmakka, who is mother of petitioners No.1 to 3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 31-01-2024 at about 2.45 p.m., the deceased Lakshmakka was proceeding in the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-4534, as an inmate, near Pothepalli village,
Bagepalli Taluk, Chikkaballapura District.

At that time, the driver of said auto-rickshaw drove the same in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, endangering to human life, lost control over his vehicle and topple to the left side of the road and caused the accident.

Due to the said impact,
the deceased has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Government Hospital, Bagepalli, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital and thereafter to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient and even after better and expert treatment she did not recover and succumbed to fatal injuries on 02-02-2024 at about 4.00 p.m. Earlier to the accident,
the deceased was working as coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Bagepalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said autorickshaw for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.

The respondent No.1 is the Narasamma vs Varalakshmi P A on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53247631/
2 owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

the insurance was in force and hence, he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

Further he has contended that, his driver was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident, vide DL No.KA5020190009323, which has been issued on 14-08-2019, valid till 13-08-2039.
He has not violated any terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further he has contended that, he has also got obtained the permission from the Transport Department and the permission is valid from 16-12-2023 to 15-12-2028.
He has denied the involvement of his vehicle and manner of accident in the alleged accident.

He has contended that, the concerned jurisdictional police have filed the charge-sheet against his vehicle, even though there is no negligence on the part of his vehicle and the entire negligence is on the part of the deceased.

The alleged accident was not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-4534,

He has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and medical expenses incurred by the petitioners.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Whereas the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.1, in respect of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-4534 and its validity as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and the said vehicle was not having valid permit.
The respondent No.1 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, he has clearly violated the policy terms and conditions as well as Motor Vehicle Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and medical expenses incurred by the petitioners.
It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident, manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-4534 as alleged in the petition.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

21. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.

sentences.text: The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are children of deceased Lakshmakka.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Lakshmakka and they were depending on her income.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased: The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 60 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of the deceased, which is marked as Ex.P.15, wherein the year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1950.
Admittedly, the accident has taken place on 31-01-2024.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 74 years.
The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and she was working as coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

But, the petitioners have not produced any document to show that,
the deceased Lakshmakka was working as coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
b) Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2024.

sentences.text: Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-B- 4534.

To establish the same the petitioners have produced certified copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.10.

As per the said document, the driver of offending vehicle by name Varalakshmi D/o Ashwathanarayanappa was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA5020190009323 to drive the said vehicle, as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was insured by respondent No.2 insurance company, vide Policy No.63010252630000, valid from 30-10-2023 to 29-10-2024.
The said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 31- 01-2024.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-40-B-4534 the said accident has occurred and the deceased Lakshmakka has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of said vehicle is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-, with simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

However, the primary liability to pay the above compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Lakshmakka, who is mother of petitioners No.1 to 3, in a road traffic accident.
At that time, the driver of said auto-rickshaw drove the same in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, endangering to human life, lost control over his vehicle and topple to the left side of the road and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact,
the deceased has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
The Bagepalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said autorickshaw for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The respondent No.1 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, he has clearly violated the policy terms and conditions as well as Motor Vehicle Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Lakshmakka has succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident, alleged to have been occurred on 31-01-2024 at about 2.45 p.m., near Pothepalli Village, Bagepalli Taluk, Chikkaballapura, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.
KA-40- B-4534 ?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto- rickshaw.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to negligence of the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on her part in the cause of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driver of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident.
There is no rebuttal evidence to show that,
the above post-mortem report is false document.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners with respect to injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and cause of her death.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-4534, injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and cause of her death.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased: The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 60 years.
a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
b) Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2024.
As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Narasamma vs Varalakshmi P A on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53247631/
8 and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 5.
As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be treated as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation under the head of parental consortium.
b ) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/- each  c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.
Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of parental consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioners No.1 to 3 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.
23.
Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
 Sl. Head of  Amount/Rs  No. Compensation
Total Rs. 8,00,000-00 Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-, with simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of said vehicle is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-, with simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- (Rupees eight lakh only) with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and  severally liable to pay the above  compensation amount to the  petitioners.
However, the primary liability to pay the above compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1- Daughter - 30% Petitioner No.2- Son - 35% Petitioner No.3- Son - 35%
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 to 3 shall be released in their favour, through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
